physical_builder_candidate: Applied Audio Products Inc. / South Plainfield facility
evidence_summary: Tone Machines reports a June 1968 factory announcement placing Applied Audio in a new South Plainfield NJ plant with Trans-Tek and states that workers there built amplifiers and effects pedals, explicitly naming the Applied Big Fuzz. This is stronger factory-operation evidence than enclosure or circuit resemblance alone.

Tone Machines reports period evidence that Applied Audio employed a predominantly female staff who built pedals and amplifiers, while workers also processed electronic components associated with Trans-Tek operations. The account names Agnes Kowalcheck in component quality work. This supports an active manufacturing workforce without assigning every Trans-Tek product to Applied.

physical_builder_candidate: Applied Audio Products Inc. / Trans-Tek shared facility
evidence_summary: The 1968 factory announcement identifies Applied Audio as an associate organization housed with Trans-Tek at the new South Plainfield NJ plant. This confirms shared-facility status but does not make Trans-Tek the pedal builder by default.

A 1970 Burnstein-Applebee catalog shows a Bowman Electronics Mod-U-Kit fuzz box whose enclosure, battery tester and knob style resemble early Applied hardware. Tone Machines notes Bowman and Trans-Tek were located near each other in Garwood, NJ, but explicitly states there is no concrete evidence connecting Bowman to Applied or proving the kit used an Applied circuit. The product must remain separate from the Applied catalog pending primary-source or internal evidence.

Tone Machines places Bowman Electronics / Bowman Leisure Industries in Roselle and Garwood NJ and describes a project-kit line sold through Lafayette Radio Electronics and Radio Shack. The geographic proximity to Trans-Tek is a lead only, not proof of common ownership or manufacture.
